notes: Six inverting op-amp stages; coords in 512-space. Op-Amp terminal order is (in+, in-, out); in EVERY op-amp here the upper input lead is the inverting one and the lower lead is the non-inverting one (see judgment call (a)). Net map: 0 = the common ground: GND 21 -> in+ of op-amp 8; GND 19 -> in+ of op-amp 0; GND 20 -> in+ of op-amp 4; GND 23 -> in+ of op-amp 1; GND 17 -> in+ of op-amp 3; GND 13 -> bottom lead of the vertical resistor 15. n1 = +15V node: V-DC(one port) 26 at (24,118) down to the horizontal at y~144, which drops at x~39 into the in- of op-amp 8 and also drops at x~107 onto the output line of op-amp 8 at y~185 (T verified at 20x), and runs right into the left lead of resistor 7 -- so in- and out of op-amp 8 are the same node. n2 = right lead of resistor 7 + in- of op-amp 2 + left lead of inductor 5 (up the x~190 riser to y~135). n3 = output of op-amp 2: the x~280 distribution column running y~133..366 -- right lead of inductor 5 (top), the op-amp 2 apex at y~185, and three taps: right at y~172 to resistor 9, right at y~276 to resistor 14, and right at y~366 to the left plate of capacitor 24. n4 = right lead of resistor 9 + in- of op-amp 4 + left lead of inductor 22 (riser at x~337). n5 = output of op-amp 4 + right lead of inductor 22 (down at x~406) + left lead of resistor 12. n6 = far-right vertical at x~507, y 169..354: right leads of resistors 12, 10 and 16. n7 = +10V node: V-DC(one port) 27 at (19,290) down to the horizontal at y~306, which branches down at x~51 into the in- of op-amp 0 and runs right into the left lead of inductor 6. n8 = output of op-amp 0 + right lead of inductor 6 + left lead of resistor 11 (all on the x~140 riser, y 263..339). n9 = right lead of resistor 11 + in+ of op-amp 2 (up the x~196 riser) + top lead of resistor 15. n10 = right lead of resistor 14 + in- of op-amp 1 + left plate of capacitor 25 (riser at x~339). n11 = output of op-amp 1 + right plate of capacitor 25 (down at x~406) + left lead of resistor 10. n12 = right plate of capacitor 24 + in- of op-amp 3 + left lead of inductor 18 (riser at x~326). n13 = output of op-amp 3 + right lead of inductor 18 (down at x~406) + left lead of resistor 16. Judgment calls: (a) input polarity. Op-amps 8, 0 and 1 carry a clearly stacked '-' above '+' inside the triangle, so upper lead = inverting; op-amps 4 and 3 show only the '+' glyph and it sits in the lower half. Op-amp 2 is the awkward one: its '+' and '-' are written side by side near the top-middle (checked at 34x) rather than stacked, so the glyph positions alone do not resolve it. It is read the same way as the rest (upper = in-, lower = in+) because that is the drafter's uniform convention and because the inductor-5 feedback path returns to the upper lead -- negative feedback. The same argument fixes op-amp 8, whose feedback also lands on the upper lead. (b) op-amp 8 has its output wired straight back to its own inverting input AND to the +15V one-port source, so in- and out share net n1. That is genuinely what is drawn (the x~107 riser was re-checked at 20x); it is not a trace error. (c) inductor 6 is drawn in the +10V rail itself: its left lead is on the same wire that feeds the in- of op-amp 0, its right lead is on the output riser, so it is the feedback element of op-amp 0 and its two terminals are on different nets (the bootstrap had both on one net). (d) resistor 15 is drawn vertically; index 0 is its top lead. All other 2-terminal parts are indexed left-then-right as drawn, capacitors left plate first. (e) no wire crossings anywhere in this sheet needed a hop/dot decision -- every intersection found is an unambiguous T.
